mutable.why: generated at first boot (cloud-init clean empties it in the image)
set by cloud-init from the instance metadata
network config rendered by cloud-init per instance
rewritten at boot with the DNS servers from DHCP
GRUB records boot state (recordfail) here at every boot; what GRUB actually loads is measured into PCRs 8-9 and checked in Phase 4

runtime.why: cloud-init instance data, including the worker bootstrap user data (its content is a Phase 4 check against the launch template)
cloud-init working directory; growpart resizes the root partition here at first boot
empty temp file cloud-init writes while rendering netplan
empty probe file written at boot to test whether / is a mount point
DHCP lease written at boot (one is left in the image from the build)
AppArmor writes its profile cache through empty temp files
snapd state; the snaps themselves are in the manifest (mounted squashfs images)
empty temp files snapd writes while refreshing its command and section caches
kubelet client and serving certificates and keys: unique per node and rotated, so checked by path only (blueprint 10.4); kubelet's config files are checked against the join reference
pod volumes, termination logs and plugin markers: workload data, not node configuration
kubelet's pod-resources socket directory
empty temp files kubelet creates for atomic writes
CSI plugin sockets and state
plugin registration sockets
device plugin sockets and checkpoint
kubelet checkpoints
CPU, memory and DRA manager state written by kubelet
allocated and actuated pod resources (in-place resize checkpoints), written by kubelet and read back when it restarts
kubelet's records of pulled images, read back when it restarts
kube-proxy ConfigMap as seen inside the kube-proxy container: a pod volume on the node's disk, so it is measured, and IMA records paths relative to the reading process's mount namespace
image content and snapshots read by containerd; files inside containers are not measured (overlayfs is excluded by the IMA policy)
Calico's kubeconfig with a service-account token that is rotated; the CNI config itself is checked against the join reference
the same kubeconfig as calico-node rewrites it through its /host/etc/cni/net.d hostPath mount when the token is refreshed (container-relative path, seen about 15 minutes after a node starts)
CNI results per pod
calico-node state
logs (journald writes while root reads, so ToMToU violations are expected here)
systemd state (random seed, timers, credentials)
logrotate's state file, read by root when logrotate.timer runs; on a worker booted more than a day after the AMI was built the persistent timer fires at boot (found in the Phase 6 run)
the temp file logrotate writes before renaming it to status
documents run by the SSM agent as root: the remote admin channel; recorded so every SSM command is visible in the log
host keys generated at first boot by cloud-init (ssh itself is masked)
nodetrust runtime state
